article_title: Data protection by design and by default

groups.reason: The policy explicitly states that privacy considerations are embedded into the design of all new products, features, and processes, and that the most privacy-protective settings are applied by default.

sub_obligations.reason: The policy explicitly states that privacy considerations are embedded into the design of all new products, features, and processes, and that the most privacy-protective settings are applied by default.

evidence.quote: Acme embeds privacy considerations into the design of all new products, features, and processes.
By default, Acme applies the most privacy-protective settings to its products.

groups.reason: The policy states that privacy-protective settings are applied by default and additional data collection requires explicit opt-in, but it does not comprehensively cover all aspects of processing extent, storage period, and accessibility by default. The policy discusses data retention schedules and access controls, but does not explicitly indicate that default-minimisation specifically applies across all four listed dimensions (amount, extent of processing, storage period, and accessibility) as a unified default principle. While the policy mentions role-based access controls and privacy-protective settings, it lacks explicit confirmation that personal data is not made accessible by default to an indefinite number of natural persons without individual intervention.

groups.principle: Certification as compliance evidence for design/default requirements
groups.reason: The policy makes no reference to holding or using an approved certification mechanism pursuant to Article 42. Per the applicability condition, this requirement applies only where the controller holds an approved certification.
